<reason>Both sides were sharp, but PRO built the cleaner path on the motion as written. The motion contrasts short-form/creator work with "traditional channel expansion," and PRO held that comparison honestly: when asked to name the loser, it answered plainly (the new/relaunched linear channel and the executive time it consumes) and then convincingly accused CON of smuggling in cuts to existing children's, minority-language and on-demand commitments that the motion does not rank. CON's counter — "nobody is launching a fifth channel, so you've won a phantom fight" — is rhetorically fun but self-harming: it concedes the comparative and does not give a reason to vote CON, while sitting in tension with CON's earlier claim that pensioners and minority-language services would be thinned. CON also conceded the goal (reach the young), conceded feed presence, and conceded the newsroom should make and publish clips, so the live dispute narrowed to ordering — precisely the ground PRO chose, where its funk example ("commissioned as the product, name on every upload") and its mechanism challenge ("a nineteen-year-old does not spontaneously download an institution") did real work. PRO also turned the Facebook-2016 analogy well (publishers lost ad revenue; a public broadcaster loses no platform revenue and can repost). CON's best live threads — market failure/abundance, credit-attribution, and creator editorial risk — were partially answered (scarce trusted impartial short-form; name on every video; contracts and existing codes), and CON's closing slightly misdescribed PRO's floor as "even if she never learns who made it" when PRO had said the broadcaster's name travels with the clip. PRO's admission that it would not invent an attribution statistic, paired with flipping the mechanism burden, was good epistemic discipline rather than evasion. CON's prose was the more memorable of the two, but rhetoric did not close the structural gap.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's [B4.1]-[B4.2] answer to CON's "name the loser" pressure: it named linear spin-off expansion outright and then showed CON was importing existing universal-service commitments the motion never ranked — turning CON's strongest pressure question into a demonstration that CON needed a comparison the motion's wording does not give it.</best_rebuttal>
